questions.question: A driving distraction is:

options.text: Anything that makes you take evasive action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving. Distractions can happen anytime and anywhere. They can cause crashes, injuries, and death.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights and a siren. You should:

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles pass. This includes police cars, fire trucks, and ambulances using sirens or flashing lights. When you see or hear one coming, pull to the right edge of the road and stop.

questions.question: As your blood alcohol content (BAC) increases, you become:
questions.correctAnswerText: More intoxicated.
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol content (BAC) measures how much alcohol is in your blood. The higher the BAC, the more impaired you are.

questions.question: If you drive faster than other vehicles and pass cars constantly on a two-lane road, you will:

options.text: Reach your destination much faster and safer.
Increase your chances of a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your chances of a crash.
questions.explanation: Avoid passing other vehicles on two-lane roads. Each time you pass, your crash risk goes up.

questions.question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads:

options.text: Your tires grip better than on pavement.
Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
You can see better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less grip than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads give your tires less grip than pavement. You must slow down. Stopping takes longer and it is easier to skid when turning.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a highway, get it off the road away from traffic if possible. Turn on your hazard lights to warn other drivers.

questions.question: Before you start the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers buckle their safety belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Make it a habit to buckle your safety belt before starting the engine. Make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: When a blind or partially blind pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street:

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only have to yield the right-of-way at corners.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians using a guide dog or carrying a white cane.

questions.question: If you become tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: If you get tired while driving, stop and rest or switch drivers. Fatigue slows your reaction time and clouds your judgment, making driving unsafe.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body and reduces its effects.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It makes you less alert, reduces your concentration, increases your reaction time, and greatly reduces your coordination.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A red and white triangular sign means you must yield the right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed on slow-moving vehicles.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange warning signs are used in work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped yellow signs indicate a no passing zone.

questions.question: What do "No passing zone" signs tell drivers?

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot legally pass another vehicle in that area. These signs are placed where it is unsafe to pass due to limited visibility.

questions.question: Why is night driving more challenging?

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, low visibility makes it difficult to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving. You can only see as far as your headlights reach.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop for them.
questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally or not at a crosswalk.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Always move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Adjust your speed to complete the turn safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning sign.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead, such as a change in traffic direction, a steep hill, or other dangerous conditions.

questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may proceed. First, check that the intersection is clear and there are no pedestrians. Then drive through at a safe speed.

questions.question: Why is using a cell phone while driving a distraction?

options.text: It makes you worry about the call cost.
It uses your hands, eyes, and mind.
It distracts other drivers on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: It uses your hands, eyes, and mind.
questions.explanation: Cell phone use while driving is dangerous. It takes your eyes, hands, and attention away from the road. Even good drivers crash more often when using a cell phone.

questions.question: How is drowsiness similar to alcohol and drugs?

options.text: It makes you a better driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: It weakens your judgment.
questions.explanation: Not getting enough sleep hurts your driving. Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness slows your reaction time, reduces awareness, and damages your judgment.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think the children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and stay stopped until the lights stop flashing. Exception: You do not need to stop if the bus is on the other side of a divided highway.

questions.question: What should you do if you encounter an aggressive driver?

options.text: Let them pass and stay out of their way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass and stay out of their way.
questions.explanation: The safest choice is to stay out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not try to compete with other drivers. Follow the rules and cooperate with everyone on the road.
